description: The bar chart illustrates the effect sizes of various multilingual BERT models across different language families and linguistic categories, with error bars indicating standard deviation. The horizontal axis categorizes the data into language families (IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other) and linguistic types (Isolate, Semitic, Uralic), while the vertical axis represents the effect size, ranging from 0 to 40. Four model types are compared: mBERT-targ (light blue), XLM-targ (dark blue), mBERT-permute (light green), and XLM-permute (dark green), as indicated by the legend. For each category, the bars show the effect size for each model, with mBERT-targ generally exhibiting the highest effect sizes, particularly in the Isolate and Uralic categories, where it reaches approximately 35. In contrast, XLM-permute consistently shows the lowest effect sizes, often near zero. The mBERT-permute and XLM-targ models show intermediate values, with XLM-targ generally higher than mBERT-permute. The error bars vary in length, indicating variability in the effect sizes, with larger errors observed in categories like IE-Indic and Uralic.
